title: A Rapid and Quantitative Fluorimetric Method for Protein-Targeting Small Molecule Drug Screening
protocol: Dissolve 30 mg of gold (III) chloride in 6.9 ml of ultrapure water to prepare 15 mM of gold (III) chloride solution.
Dissolve 74 mg of HSA or BSA in 1 ml of ultrapure water to prepare a 74 mg/ml protein stock solution.
Dissolve 1.9 mg of ibuprofen, 2.8 mg of warfarin, 2.3 mg of phenytoin, and 1.5 mg of sulfanilamide in 20 μl of DMSO to prepare their respective drug stock solutions at 450 mM.
Dissolve 600 mg of NaOH pellets in 10 ml of ultrapure water to prepare 1.5 M of NaOH solution.
Dissolve 2.4 g of urea in 2 ml of ultrapure water to prepare 20 M of urea solution.
Place two glass vials, each containing a micro magnetic stir bar, on separate temperature controllable magnetic stirrers.
Set the temperature of one magnetic stirrer to 60 °C and label its vial as “60 °C”.
Keep the other magnetic stirrer at room temperature (RT) with its vial labeled as “RT”.
Add 200 µl of HSA solution, 200 µl of ultrapure water, and 200 µl of gold (III) chloride solution to each vial under constant stirring (360 rpm).
Add 20 μl of NaOH solution to each vial after 2 min.
Start recording the reaction time as 0 min.
Draw 50 μl of solutions from each sample every 20 min and measure the emission spectrum with a microplate reader.
Stop the magnetic stirrer after 100 min.
Cool down the glass vials under running water in a sink.
Place a glass vial containing a micro magnetic stir bar on top of a magnetic stirrer.
Mix 200 µl of BSA solution, 75 µl of gold (III) chloride solution, and 75 µl of urea in the glass vial under constant stirring.
Add 20 µl of NaOH solution to activate the reducing capability of BSA for Au NC formation.
Start recording reaction time as 0 min after adding NaOH.
Measure photoemission spectrum of the reaction mixture hourly.
Plot the photoemission spectra at all times to observe the formation kinetics of Au NCs by urea denaturation.
Place five glass vials, each containing a magnetic stir bar, on top of a temperature controllable multipoint magnetic stirrer.
Label four vials for drugs (ibuprofen, warfarin, phenytoin, sulfanilamide) and one as control for pure HSA.
Add 200 µl of HSA to each vial.
Add 1 µl of drug solution to the four corresponding vials.
Add 1 µl of DMSO to the control vial.
Switch on the stirrer and set the spin speed to 360 rpm.
Incubate for 1 hr under constant stirring to allow drug binding to HSA.
Add 200 µl of Milli-Q water to each vial under constant stirring.
Add 200 µl of gold (III) chloride solution to each vial under constant stirring.
Set the temperature to 60 °C and stir for 10 min.
Add 20 µl of 1.5 M NaOH to each vial.
Start recording reaction time as 0 min.
Draw 50 µl of solution from each vial into a 384-well black plate.
Measure the emission spectrum (results labeled as 0 min).
Record the emission spectra of each sample every 10 min.
Collect at least four spectra at 0, 10, 20, and 30 min.
Repeat steps to obtain consistent results.
Stop the magnetic stirrer.
Plot time-resolved photoemission spectra for each sample.
Identify peak intensity of all samples and plot against time.
Measure the binding constant of a specific drug to HSA.
Replace drug solution with ibuprofen solutions at four different concentrations.
Label glass vials according to ibuprofen concentration correspondingly.
Cool down the glass vials under running water in a sink for 10 minutes.
Wear heat resistant gloves when handling the hot glass vials.
Pipette 50 μl of each solution from the vial into a 384-well black plate.
Measure the emission spectrum of the solutions in the plate.
Repeat steps to obtain another two sets of results at different drug concentrations.
Stop the magnetic stirrer after completing measurements.
Plot the photoemission spectra using software such as OriginPro software.
Find out the peak intensity for each sample's photoemission spectra.
Calculate and plot the relative fluorescence intensity [(I0 - I) /I0] against the drug concentration.
Fit the data to a single site binding model using the Michaelis-Menten equation: Y = Rmax × C/(KD + C).
Perform nonlinear curve fit in software such as OriginPro.
Select Hill function from Growth/Sigmoidal category for fitting.
Click Fit on the Settings: Function Selection page to show up the fitted results.
